labels.description: Adds a new sentence disclosing that in certain circumstances AT&T could be liable for the actions of its suppliers and other third parties it does business with.
labels.rationale: criterion 1: a new exposure (third-party liability for supplier and partner conduct) is disclosed that was absent in the prior year.

labels.description: The only difference is removal of a stray page number (11) between paragraphs; the risk factor text is otherwise identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-number artifact only, no change in substance, likelihood, scope or figures.

labels.description: The as-of date rolls forward from December 31, 2024 to December 31, 2025 while the union-represented share of the workforce stays at approximately 43%.
labels.rationale: minor: routine date roll-forward only; the 43% figure and the named unions (CWA, IBEW) are unchanged.

labels.description: The risk factor is widened from business transformation initiatives to also cover acquisitions, joint ventures, dispositions and investments (notably those aimed at enhancing fiber serviceable locations), and adds that AI-related laws are uncertain and vary by jurisdiction and that AI may not meaningfully enhance products or operations.
labels.rationale: criterion 2 and criterion 3: new business activities (acquisitions, joint ventures, dispositions, fiber-location investments) and AI regulation are referenced, and the scope of the risk is widened.

labels.description: Adds that AT&T may be subject to injunctions, alongside paying amounts or changing operations, as a result of unfavorable litigation or government charges.
labels.rationale: criterion 1 and criterion 3: a new remedy exposure (injunctive relief) is disclosed, widening the scope of the litigation risk.

labels.description: Changes "Cyberattacks can cause" equipment failures, data loss and disruptions to "Cyberattacks have caused, and may in the future cause" them, and states such attacks "have and in the future could" result in significant expenses, investigations, liability, customer loss and reputational damage; the rest is "the Company" to "we" rewording.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the characterization moves from hypothetical to realized harm, even though the "the Company" to "we" edits are stylistic.

labels.description: The only difference is a page number (12) inserted mid-paragraph by the page break; the text is otherwise identical.
labels.rationale: minor: page-number artifact only, no change in substance.

labels.description: Changes "We have incurred debt to fund significant acquisitions" and spectrum purchases to "We intend to and have incurred debt" for them, adding a forward-looking intent to take on more acquisition and spectrum debt, and drops "going forward" from the debt-management goal.
labels.rationale: criterion 3: the risk moves from a past fact to a stated intention to incur further debt, widening the scope; the "going forward" deletion alone would be stylistic.

labels.description: Drops the named examples of tax laws whose application may be uncertain, the U.S. Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 and the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022; the remaining text is unchanged apart from a page number.
labels.rationale: criterion 2: two specifically named regulations are dropped from the disclosure.

labels.description: Covered the risk that the WarnerMedia distribution and related transactions could fail to qualify as tax-free on IRS audit despite a favorable Private Letter Ruling, leaving AT&T with significant tax liability subject only to indemnification from Warner Bros. Discovery and its credit risk.
